Checkup

Inphinit features a tool that assists in diagnosing the environment, identifying potential issues or suggesting optimal configurations—such as those aimed at enhancing security or performance.

Using

It is possible to use the class to detect problems in the environment where the application is running, like this:

<?php use Inphinit\Diagnostics\Checkup; $app->action('GET', '/checkup', function () { $check = new Checkup(); $errors = $check->getErrors(); echo implode("<br>\n", $errors); $warnings = $check->getWarnings(); echo implode("<br>\n", $warnings); });

When creating a new project, the /checkup in main.php route will already be configured and working to determine the conditions of the environment in which the application is running. It's possible to move the route to a context with authentication or limit it to the scope of a private host. Related files:

  • system/
    • Controllers/
      • CheckupController.php
    • views/
      • checkup.php

These files can be removed or completely recreated; the approach presented is just a sample of basic usage.
